description: First trilateral Maritime Security Belt naval exercise opens in the Gulf of Oman and northern Indian Ocean.
notes: Start of the annual trilateral series.

description: Foreign ministers Wang Yi and Zarif sign a 25-year comprehensive cooperation agreement in Tehran; full text not published.
notes: Negotiated since Xi's 2016 visit to Tehran.

description: Xi and Putin issue a joint statement in Beijing declaring a partnership with 'no limits' and no 'forbidden' areas of cooperation.
notes: Twenty days before Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

description: China and Russia jointly veto a US-drafted UNSC resolution tightening DPRK sanctions after ICBM tests; 13 members voted in favour.
notes: First P5 split on a DPRK sanctions resolution since 2006.

description: Iran begins transferring Shahed- and Mohajer-series drones to Russia; the White House later said several hundred had been delivered by mid-2023.
notes: Iran says it supplied only a small number of drones and only before the invasion; it denies supplying weapons for use in Ukraine.

description: White House says a small number of IRGC personnel are in occupied Crimea supporting Russian Shahed-136 launches.
Declassified US intelligence says Iran is supplying materials for a plant in Russia's Alabuga SEZ to produce Iranian-designed attack drones.
Iran becomes the ninth full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, joining China and Russia.
Kim Jong Un and Putin hold a summit at the Vostochny Cosmodrome; Kim pledges full support for Russia.
Iran's full membership of BRICS takes effect.
Maritime Security Belt 2024 trilateral naval drill.
notes: Day not yet coded; refine from primary MoD sources.

description: Russia vetoes renewal of the UN 1718 Committee Panel of Experts monitoring DPRK sanctions (13 in favour; China abstained).
notes: Panel mandate ended 30 April 2024.

description: China abstains on the Panel of Experts renewal that Russia vetoes.
notes: Coded separately from CRK-0012 to keep vetoes and abstentions distinct.

description: US officials say China supplied about 70% of Russia's machine-tool imports (Q4 2023) and about 90% of its microelectronics, feeding Russian weapons production.
notes: China denies providing lethal aid and calls this normal trade.

description: North Korean delegation led by External Economic Relations Minister Yun Jong Ho leaves for a rare publicly announced visit to Iran.
notes: Seoul and Washington voiced concern about missile cooperation; Tehran said the visit was economic.

description: Putin and Kim sign the Treaty on Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in Pyongyang, including a mutual assistance clause.
notes: Some sources give 18 June; Interfax and KCNA give 19 June.

description: In 2024, up to 9 million artillery and MRL rounds were shipped in 49 deliveries, along with at least 100 KN-23/KN-24 ballistic missiles and heavy artillery and MRL systems, per the MSMT.
notes: Report by 11 states (UN doc S/2025/340). OSC gives a lower estimate of 4.2–5.8m rounds (Aug 2023–Mar 2025).

description: Russia supplies short-range air defence (incl. at least one Pantsir) and electronic warfare systems to North Korea from November 2024, per the MSMT.
More than one million barrels of refined petroleum delivered in 43 tanker arrivals (Mar–Oct 2024), over twice the UN cap of 500,000 bbl/yr, per the MSMT citing OSC/BBC.
US says Russia has received Iranian Fath-360 close-range ballistic missiles and that Russian personnel trained on them in Iran; new US/E3 sanctions follow.
notes: Iran's foreign minister denied any delivery.

description: North Korea deploys over 11,000 troops to Russia, who fight in Kursk region; both governments confirm this in April 2025.
notes: Coded A because both participants confirmed (Russia 26 Apr, DPRK 28 Apr 2025). MSMT reports 3,000+ reinforcements Jan–Mar 2025.

description: The Russia–DPRK Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty, with its mutual military assistance commitment, enters into force on exchange of ratifications in Moscow.
notes: Replaces the 2000 friendship treaty; unlimited duration.

description: Putin and Pezeshkian sign the Russia–Iran Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty in Moscow.
notes: No mutual-defence clause. Iran's MFA gives the date as 16 January.

description: Maritime Security Belt 2025 exercise off Chabahar in the Gulf of Oman (about 10–15 March).
notes: Sources disagree on start day, so coded to the month.

description: After meeting Kim in Pyongyang, Shoigu announces that North Korea will send 1,000 deminers and 5,000 military construction troops to Kursk region.
notes: Shoigu's third Pyongyang visit in three months.

description: Xi and Putin hold talks at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing.
notes: Replace with Kremlin/MFA readout on the next update.

description: Xi hosts Putin, Kim and Pezeshkian at the Beijing parade marking 80 years since the end of WWII, the first event attended by all four leaders.
notes: Symbolic event; low intensity by design (see CODEBOOK).

description: Xi and Kim hold talks in Beijing and pledge closer ties.
Russia and China vote to continue Iran's UNSCR 2231 sanctions relief after the E3 trigger snapback; the draft fails 4–9.
notes: Algeria and Pakistan also voted in favour.

description: Russia and China table a draft to delay snapback by six months; it fails 4–9–2 and UN sanctions on Iran return on 28 September.
The Russia–Iran Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty enters into force, according to both foreign ministries.
notes: Iran's ambassador had called it binding in July 2025; Russia's MFA gives 2 October. 20-year term.

description: Premier Li Qiang visits Pyongyang (9–11 Oct) for the Workers' Party of Korea 80th anniversary.
notes: Party-and-government delegation on an official goodwill visit.

description: A Russian delegation led by Dmitry Medvedev attends the WPK 80th anniversary celebrations and parade in Pyongyang.
China is effectively the sole buyer of Iranian crude exports in 2025, keeping Iran's oil revenue flowing despite US sanctions (tanker-tracking data).
notes: USCC (Mar 2026) puts China's share at upward of 90%. This is a continuous flow, coded as one event per year.

description: A Ukrainian intelligence assessment reviewed by Reuters says Russian satellites imaged dozens of Middle East sites to help Iranian targeting during the US–Israel war, and that Russian and Iranian hackers cooperated.
notes: Reuters could not independently confirm. A Western military source and a regional source told Reuters imagery was shared. Reported 7 Apr 2026.

description: Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui meets Putin at the Kremlin; Putin thanks North Korean troops for their war contribution.
Ukraine says it struck Caspian Sea cargo vessels (Port Olya 2, Begey) used to carry military cargo between Russia and Iran; Iran says a commercial ship was hit and a sailor killed.
notes: Direction disputed (Iran→Russia vs Russia→Iran), so sender/receiver left blank. Evidence of an active military supply corridor.

description: Russia and China veto a US-backed resolution to extend the mandate of the UN panel of experts monitoring Iran sanctions (11 in favour; Pakistan and Somalia abstained).
notes: Panel was reinstated by the 2025 snapback but never staffed.

description: WPK Secretary Jo Yong Won, a close Kim aide, meets Putin in Moscow ahead of the US–China–Russia leaders' meeting.
Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen on the sidelines of APEC, the day before the first US–China–Russia leaders' meeting.
